samples.summary: Merge spans read from the shared (peer-writable) document are never bounds-checked, and the new paste path iterates them cell-by-cell (`mergeCoveredSrefs` / `clearCellsUnderMerge`), giving a hostile collaborator another way to freeze another user's client
samples.evidence: `Sheet.merges` is populated verbatim from the collaborative document (`loadMerges` → `store.getMerges`, sheet.ts:507; yorkie-store.ts:997 copies `{...span}` with no validation of `rs`/`cs`), and nothing in `packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-record.ts` or the store layer clamps a span to the sheet or to the anchor's remaining rows/cols. The new code in `paste` iterates every covered cell of every intersecting block: sheet.ts:2334 (`for (const sref of this.mergeCoveredSrefs(merge.anchor, merge.span))` for each overwritten/cut block) and sheet.ts:2343 → `clearCellsUnderMerge` (sheet.ts:927-965), which additionally performs an `await this.store.get(ref)` per covered cell. Attack: a peer with write access (or a tampered document/import) writes `merges["A1"] = { rs: 1e9, cs: 1e9 }`; any subsequent paste whose destination range touches A1 spins ~1e18 iterations plus one store read each inside a `beginBatch`, wedging the victim's renderer and leaving the batch open. Availability only — no data disclosure. I could not confirm this is *newly* exploitable: `rebuildMergeCoverMap` (sheet.ts:780-792) already walks the same unvalidated spans at document load, so the same hostile span likely hangs the client before a paste is even possible; the new path is an additional, cheaper-to-trigger amplifier. Hardening: validate `rs`/`cs` when merges are read from the store (or clamp in `mergeCoveredSrefs`).
searchedFor: grep setMerge|deleteMerge|getMerges across packages/sheets/src and packages/frontend

samples.summary: The new merge propagation updates in-memory merge state unconditionally, ignoring that the store layer may have refused the write (ReadOnlyStore no-ops `setMerge` and returns `false` from `deleteMerge`)
samples.evidence: sheet.ts:2337-2342 does `await this.store.deleteMerge(merge.anchor); this.merges.delete(...)` and `await this.store.setMerge(...); this.merges.set(...)` without inspecting the result. `packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts:256-262` implements `setMerge` as a silent no-op and `deleteMerge` as `return false`, i.e. the store is the write-refusal layer for read-only-backed sheets. A `Sheet` built on that store (or any store that rejects the write) will still show and act on merge geometry that was never persisted, and `clearCellsUnderMerge` will still delete/strip covered cells locally. The user-facing entry points are gated (`Spreadsheet.paste` checks `_readOnly` at spreadsheet.ts:690; the Ctrl-V keybinding checks `this.readOnly` at worksheet.ts:5094), and the backend Yorkie auth webhook is the real authority, so I could not turn this into an enforcement bypass — it is defense-in-depth being bypassed for embedders that rely on a refusing store rather than on the view-layer flag. Same pattern already exists in `mergeSelection` (sheet.ts:4499-4500) and `moveRangeTo` (sheet.ts:2562), so this is a propagation of an existing habit, not a new hole.
